claude.request:
Today's international headlines:
- South Carolina elects Democratic senator for first time in almost three decades: Annie Andrews is projected to defeat Darline Graham, who was handpicked by President Trump to take her brother's seat after his death.
- Democratic rising star Ossoff projected to hold Georgia seat: Ossoff is seen as a potential leading contender for the Democratic nomination for president in 2028 if he throws his hat in the ring.
- Spanish transport minister resigns days after deadly train crash: At least 69 people were killed and dozens injured in the collision south of the capital, Madrid.
- Seven flights across Europe targeted by suspected bomb threats: Planes in Poland, Spain, Bulgaria and Italy have been checked for explosives following separate threats.
- Weapon or wine bottle? China disputes reports of artillery shell in Papua New Guinea: Papua New Guinea police had earlier dismissed speculation that the 32kg object was "merely a dummy".
- Binance says fake job interviews used as part of $6.3bn crypto hack: An engineer was contacted through a legitimate job-hunting platform and invited to bogus job interviews with fake company representatives, Binance says.
- NTSB says crucial plane parts found three miles from Florida crash site: The NTSB said because the parts were found far from the accident site, they fell off before the crash.
- Europe on alert after supermarket freezers hit by cyber-attacks in 10 countries: Supermarkets have reported problems from Estonia and Sweden to Portugal and Italy and many retainers have been forced to discard food.
- Libya's top religious authority rules against wearing Nike clothes: The US company was named after the Greek goddess of victory, so the Dar al-Ifta said displaying its logo was unIslamic.
- Death toll rises in Ukraine after Russia attacks aid centre, hospice and hospital: At least 38 people are killed in 24 hours and Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky warns dozens more could be trapped under rubble.
- Indian tourist killed after two helicopters collide near Everest base camp: The two aircraft crashed just metres from the ground after trying to land at the same spot.
- Irish Olympian Ciara Mageean was a 'talented and inspirational human being': The former European champion and two-time Olympic runner had been diagnosed with stage four bowel cancer.
